items.title: CVE-2026-105769 — kaniko can send the build's Azure (Entra ID) access token to lookalike ACR registry hosts
items.body:
Vulnérabilité critique CVE-2026-105769 affectant github.com/chainguard-dev/kaniko (go) (score CVSS 9.3).

kaniko can send the build's Azure (Entra ID) access token to lookalike ACR registry hosts

The flaw is in the Azure Container Registry (ACR) credential helper, github.com/chrismellard/docker-credential-acr-env . kaniko links it into the executor and warmer (the built-in helper) and also builds it as the standalone docker-credential-acr-env binary.
items.detail:
Vulnérabilité critique CVE-2026-105769 affectant github.com/chainguard-dev/kaniko (go) (score CVSS 9.3).

kaniko can send the build's Azure (Entra ID) access token to lookalike ACR registry hosts

The flaw is in the Azure Container Registry (ACR) credential helper, github.com/chrismellard/docker-credential-acr-env . kaniko links it into the executor and warmer (the built-in helper) and also builds it as the standalone docker-credential-acr-env binary. The helper decides whether a host is an ACR registry with an unanchored regex, so any hostname that contains .azurecr.io (or .azurecr.cn , .azurecr.de , .azurecr.us ) passes. The upstream module is unmaintained and has no fixed release. The Go vulnerability database tracks the upstream flaw as GO-2026-6225 .

You are affected if you run kaniko before v1.25.20 on Dockerfiles, or build arguments, that you don't fully control, in an environment where the helper can get an Azure identity:

You do not need to use ACR, or configure the helper, to be affected. kaniko consults the built-in helper for any registry that has no credentials in your Docker config and is not a Google or Amazon ECR registry, and every lookalike host falls in that set. That covers base images in FROM lines and images in COPY --from= . kaniko asks for credentials before it contacts the registry, so the attacker's registry doesn't need to request authentication.

If your Docker config.json sets "credsStore": "acr-env" , the standalone binary is consulted for every registry as well. Before v1.25.20 this setting broke pulls from non-ACR registries, so it is uncommon.

The helper puts the token in both the Authorization: Bearer header and the access_token form field of a POST to https:// /oauth2/exchange , so the attacker receives a live access token for Azure

items.title: Get root on a musl Linux system by slamming it with an overly long password
items.body:
Vulnérabilité critique affectant Linux.

On certain Linux systems, an attacker could gain root access by entering a password longer than 256 bytes. The vulnerability, dubbed *sshole by Wakefield researcher Özgün Kültekin, who discovered it, can only be exploited in very specific conditions.
items.detail:
Vulnérabilité critique affectant Linux.

On certain Linux systems, an attacker could gain root access by entering a password longer than 256 bytes. The vulnerability, dubbed *sshole by Wakefield researcher Özgün Kültekin, who discovered it, can only be exploited in very specific conditions. The flaw affects certain Linux systems using musl libc instead of the traditional GNU C library, and even then only those running OpenSSH's secure shell daemon without Pluggable Authentication Modules (PAM) and with password authentication enabled. If those conditions are met, and at least one other account has a valid password hash, accounts that shouldn't accept passwords, such as root, key-only deployment users, and LDAP users, may be accessed by supplying a password between 257 and 1,024 characters. The targeted accounts must have an asterisk (*) in their password field, and direct root login remains subject to OpenSSH's configuration. That might seem niche, but sorry: It’s not. Musl libc is common in embedded Linux systems due to its low footprint. More critically than that, it's also the standard C library for Alpine Linux, which provides official cloud images for both AWS and Azure. Some Alpine systems running in those environments may therefore be vulnerable, depending on their configuration. items.title: CVE-2026-12411 — lxd allows Cross-guest volume hijack via DevLXD device patch
items.body:
Vulnérabilité élevée CVE-2026-12411 affectant github.com/canonical/lxd (go) (score CVSS 8.4).

lxd allows Cross-guest volume hijack via DevLXD device patch

Volumes created over DevLXD get volatile.devlxd.owner set to the calling identity. The storage handlers enforce it on GET / PUT / DELETE ( isDevLXDVolumeOwner , lxd/devlxd_storage.go:359 ) and on volume-copy sources ( devlxd_storage.go:286 ).
items.detail:
Vulnérabilité élevée CVE-2026-12411 affectant github.com/canonical/lxd (go) (score CVSS 8.4).

lxd allows Cross-guest volume hijack via DevLXD device patch

Volumes created over DevLXD get volatile.devlxd.owner set to the calling identity. The storage handlers enforce it on GET / PUT / DELETE ( isDevLXDVolumeOwner , lxd/devlxd_storage.go:359 ) and on volume-copy sources ( devlxd_storage.go:286 ). The device-attach path does not.

devLXDInstancePatchHandler ( lxd/devlxd_instances.go:88 ) passes the guest's device map to generateDevLXDInstanceDevices ( devlxd_instances.go:178 ). For a device that isn't already on the instance, the only check is isDeviceAccessible(device) :

if ( exists && ! isOwned ) || ( ! isDeviceAccessible ( device )) exists is false for a newly added device, so isDeviceAccessible is the whole gate. It resolves to newDevLXDDeviceAccessValidator ( devlxd_instances.go:250 ), which is diskDeviceAllowed && filters.IsCustomVolumeDisk(device) . IsCustomVolumeDisk ( lxd/device/filters/disk.go:28 ) checks the device shape only: type=disk , non-empty source , non-empty pool . It never loads the (pool, source) volume or compares its owner to the caller.

The handler then sets volatile. .devlxd.owner to the caller and issues an in-process PATCH to instancePatch ( lxd/instance_patch.go:55 ). That call skips the HTTP access handler and runs only project quota checks ( limits.AllowInstanceUpdate , instance_patch.go:215 ) before c.Update . The disk device's validateConfig confirms the volume exists but does no ownership or RBAC check. A guest can therefore point a new disk device at any custom volume in its project and LXD mounts it. The recorded device owner becomes the attacker while the volume's volatile.devlxd.owner still names the victim.

Incident de sécurité rapporté par Infosecurity Mag.

Bitdefender warns that unfixed GhostMap bug could force users to factory reset their device

Security experts have warned of a new vulnerability in Android smartphones which could plunge devices into a crash loop that can only be fixed by forcing a factory reset.

items.detail:
Incident de sécurité rapporté par Infosecurity Mag.

Bitdefender warns that unfixed GhostMap bug could force users to factory reset their device

Security experts have warned of a new vulnerability in Android smartphones which could plunge devices into a crash loop that can only be fixed by forcing a factory reset.

Bitdefender said it discovered the issue when an Android package (APK) it collected from the wild crashed the emulators in its labs. It found that the problem wasn’t malware, but a bug in the Android OS itself.

“The operating system mishandles two fields inside a ZIP entry, the compression method and the declared uncompressed length. Reading such an entry causes a SIGBUS (a signal sent by the CPU to stop a process that accesses an invalid memory space) in whichever process touches the file,” it explained in a blog post.

“We call it GhostMap: the malformed entry causes Android to map the file across memory that was never allocated, and the crash occurs when a process reads from that empty space.”

Read more on Android bugs: Google API Keys Quietly Gain Access to Gemini on Android Devices.

Bitdefender said that the crash loop persists after a reboot and continues in safe mode, meaning the only way out is a factory reset which erases all locally stored data.

Signal de veille — The Record.

The sanctions target four people and 41 companies linked to the Prince Group — a Cambodian company accused of running a billion-dollar scam operation.

The Treasury Department on Thursday sanctioned dozens of people and companies tied to scam compounds in Cambodia, Madagascar and several other countries across Southeast Asia and Africa.

The sanctions target four people and 41 companies linked to the Prince Group — a Cambodian company accused of running a billion-dollar scam operation.

The company is accused of running hundreds of compounds in Cambodia where workers and human trafficking victims were forced to conduct cyberscams and steal billions of dollars from people in the U.S., Europe and China. Prince Group was dismantled earlier this year after its CEO was arrested and extradited to China .

Treasury Department officials argued that the new measures are needed because Prince Group employees have tried to evade two previous rounds of sanctions by offloading funds to shell companies, relatives or assistants in an effort to maintain access to scam funds.

“Rather than operating through a single corporate structure, senior Prince Group TCO executives have relied on layers of offshore holding companies, foreign entities, nominee directors, and corporate service providers to maintain control over assets while obscuring beneficial ownership,” the Treasury Department said.

“Today’s designations target key components of that network, including companies and individuals that have facilitated corporate administration, managed offshore entities, and provided business services to senior Prince Group TCO officials.”

Trellix observed a 41.4% drop in China-nexus activity between April and September, which may reflect changing PRC strategic priorities

Chinese nation-state threat activity declined by 41.4% in the six months from April to September 2026, according to a new study by Trellix.

The researchers said the significant fall in detected activity could be linked to broader geopolitical developments and shifting People’s Republic of China (PRC) intelligence priorities.

These may include having a greater focus on observing Western military capabilities, such as battlefield technologies.

Overall, Chinese-aligned detection trends broadly coincided with changes in Chinese military and maritime activity around Taiwan. For example, cyber activity rose slightly from June to July 2026 at the same time as China expanded coast guard-led ‘gray-zone’ operations around the Island.

This activity includes reports of Chinese coast guard ships patrolling Taiwan-controlled waters.

Despite the sharp fall in China-aligned detections, observed PRC cyber activity remained “substantially higher” than nation-state cyber activity from Russia and Iran during the period, the researchers noted.
